statement: Compression profiles exist only in the creation-time planner; the native reader decodes from recorded TransformPlans and operational codecs and never consults the planner module.
refines_or_supersedes: CONTRIBUTING.md L67-70 (decoder depends only on recorded TransformPlans)
evidence_in_source: module doc; readers (ecf/container.rs, ecf/random.rs) import codec not planner

statement: UNPLANNED_PLAN_ID = 0 is a temporary plan_ref marker used between plaintext chunking and planning.
Public planner constants: ZSTD_ATTRIBUTABLE_OVERHEAD_BYTES = 16, MINIMUM_GAIN_BYTES = 32, MINIMUM_GAIN_BASIS_POINTS = 100 (one percent) govern when a non-STORE plan may win.
research_needed: Sensitivity sweep of gain thresholds on a representative corpus (size vs decode CPU).

statement: Private planner constants: MINIMUM_ZSTD_INPUT_BYTES 64, PROBE_BYTES 4096, MINIMUM_COHORT_GAIN_BYTES 128, dictionary/chunk-group/reconstruction section overhead 64 bytes each, MINIMUM_RECONSTRUCTION_GAIN_BYTES 256 and 200 basis points.

All planner acceptance margins (32 B/1% codec, 128 B cohort, 256 B/2% reconstruction, fixed 64-byte section charges) are hard-coded numeric choices with no cited measurement of size, CPU, or access-cost trade-offs.
research_needed: Parameter sweep on real corpora measuring final archive size, pack/unpack CPU and random-access cost under alternative margins.
decision_needed: Are the frozen v6 margins acceptable for v1 or must a new planner version retune them from measurements?

statement: Frozen v1-v3 Zstandard level sets: fast [1]; balanced [1,3,5] with fallback [1] when the probe predicts incompressible data; dense [5,9,15]; extreme [9,15,19,22].
CompressionProfile has exactly four public variants (fast, balanced, dense, extreme); Balanced is the Default.
Planner IDs are frozen per profile and version: <profile>-v1 through -v6; planner_id() returns the -v6 ID used for all new filesystem archives, with accessors for each historical ID.
refines_or_supersedes: CONTRIBUTING.md L67-70, L85-99 (planner behavior frozen by ID)

statement: Ordered CDC candidates per profile: fast [FAST_V2]; balanced [BALANCED_V2]; dense [BALANCED_V2, DENSE_V2]; extreme [FAST_V2, BALANCED_V2, DENSE_V2, EXTREME_V2]; earlier candidates win complete-cost ties.
In v1-v3 selection the content probe gates Zstandard levels only for fast (no Zstandard if incompressible) and balanced (level 1 only); dense and extreme try all their levels regardless of the probe.

Profile cross-file policies: dictionary levels fast none, balanced 3/5, dense 5/9/15, extreme 9/15/19; lookback candidates fast/balanced none, dense 1/2/4 at levels 5/9, extreme 1/2/4/8 at levels 9/15/19.

from_planner_id recognizes only -v1..-v6 IDs, yet encrypted packing overwrites planner_id with '<profile>-enc-v1' after v6 planning; the underlying planner version is not recorded and explain falls back to plaintext-length baselines for encrypted archives.
research_needed: Verify explain/inspect output for encrypted archives; enumerate planner changes that would silently reuse '*-enc-v1'.
decision_needed: Should encrypted planner IDs encode the underlying planner version (e.g., balanced-v6-enc-v1)?

statement: Profile parsing accepts only fast|balanced|dense|extreme; anything else yields PolicyRefused/CommandUsage (EB_CLI_USAGE). No codec, level, chunk-size or dictionary override is exposed.
decision_needed: Should expert overrides (codec/level/chunk size) exist in v1, or remain deliberately absent?

statement: Public ContentAnalysis (length, sample length, distinct symbols, max-symbol ppm, adjacent-repeat ppm, likely_compressible) and PlanningReport (per-codec chunk counts, transformed/dictionary/lookback/reconstructive counts, cohorts, attempts, cost rejections, selected plans).

Historical planners remain callable: public plan_archive (frozen v1 fixed-chunk selection) and plan_archive_v2 (post-CDC) clear reconstruction and whole-object state before selecting, so the library can still create *-v1 and *-v2 archives.
decision_needed: Should creation of historical planner versions remain in the public library API after v1 freeze?

statement: plan_archive_v3 runs v1-style independent STORE/Zstandard selection, then cross-file cohort planning, and always sets FEATURE_CROSS_FILE_COMPRESSION_V1 while clearing the codec-transform bit.
plan_archive_v4 competes registered independent codec/transform pipelines per chunk, then applies frozen v3 cross-file strategies; it unconditionally requires feature bits 0x1 and 0x2.
plan_archive_v5 adds verified DEFLATE reconstruction before v3 cohort strategies; bit 0x4 is set whenever ReconstructionData or any fallback audit record exists.
plan_archive_v6 first runs the complete v5 planner, sets the -v6 planner ID and clears region/audit state; fast-v6 returns immediately with no JPEG attempts.

V6 per-ContentObject eligibility order: no chunks -> NotRecognized; balanced with more than one chunk -> ResourcePolicyExcluded; more than 4096 chunks -> ResourcePolicyExcluded; chunk shared by another ContentObject, grouped, or dictionary-planned -> RegionDedupConflict.

V6 records ChunkGroup membership and Dictionary plans under the RegionDedupConflict audit reason, so persisted audits cannot distinguish true cross-object dedup conflicts from cross-file planning conflicts.
decision_needed: Should a future audit schema separate dedup conflicts from dictionary/group conflicts?

statement: Because v5 cohort planning (dictionaries, lookback) runs before JPEG region selection and grouped or dictionary chunks are then ineligible, similar JPEG chunks placed in cohorts may lose larger whole-object JPEG savings.
research_needed: Measure on JPEG-heavy corpora how often cohort assignment blocks a region and the size difference versus region-first planning.
decision_needed: Should a future planner select JPEG regions before similarity cohorts?

statement: V6 materializes the full ContentObject in memory, excludes objects over MAX_JPEG_BYTES (64 MiB), and maps verified_forward failures to NotRecognized, Unsupported, ExactVerificationFailed or ResourcePolicyExcluded audits.

V6 region cost = post-codec representation + TransformPlan v3 record if new + region record + section header for the first region only; baseline = existing v5 payload bytes of unique member chunks; region must save more than max(256 B, 2%); ties keep ordinary.

V6 does not prune v5 TransformPlans left unused after member chunks move to a region, and its ordinary baseline excludes plan-record bytes; the first-region-only section-header charge makes selection depend on ContentObject digest order.
evidence_in_source: inference from code (plans map rebuilt without used-plan retain)
research_needed: Measure orphaned plan-record bytes and any selection differences caused by order-dependent section-header charges.

statement: Selected regions get region_id from jpeg_reconstruction::region_identity; member chunks get plan_ref REGION_MEMBER_PLAN_REF (0), lose group_ref, and their v5 fallback records are removed.

The planner never checks the 64:1 region expansion bound or representation limits that EAM validation enforces, so a highly compressible JPEG region could be selected and then fail encoding (ResourceLimit) instead of falling back.
research_needed: Construct a JPEG with large compressible APP/COM segments and pack with dense/extreme; observe pack failure vs fallback.
decision_needed: Should planner eligibility mirror every validation bound before selection?

statement: V6 sets feature bits 0x1|0x2|0x4|0x8 whenever any region or any audit exists, and an audit is inserted for every non-selected ContentObject, including non-JPEG and empty objects.

Consequently nearly every non-fast v6 archive carries per-ContentObject JPEG audit records and requires the whole-object-reconstruction feature bit even when no JPEG exists, so readers lacking 0x8 refuse ordinary archives and audit bytes scale with object count.
evidence_in_source: inference from code; tests check audits only for JPEG fixtures
research_needed: Pack non-JPEG corpora (many small files) with balanced/dense; measure audit bytes per object and feature bits set.
decision_needed: Should feature bits reflect only techniques actually selected, and should audits be emitted only for recognized candidates?

statement: V5 records a ReconstructionFallback for every non-reconstructive chunk in non-fast profiles, so bit 0x4 and per-chunk fallback records appear in almost all balanced/dense/extreme archives regardless of DEFLATE content.
evidence_in_source: inference from code; tests/reconstructive_transform.rs:139-163 shows fallback on non-DEFLATE chunk
research_needed: Measure fallback record bytes per chunk and share of archives requiring bit 0x4.
decision_needed: Is per-chunk fallback evidence worth its physical overhead and the compatibility cost of an always-required feature bit?

statement: After v6 the PlanningReport's per-codec counters still reflect the pre-region v5 assignment, reconstructive_chunks counts region members, and reconstruction_attempts mixes per-chunk v5 attempts with per-object v6 attempts.
JPEG XL post-codec candidates: balanced STORE, LZ4, Zstandard 3/5; dense STORE, Zstandard 9/15, LZMA2 6/4 MiB; extreme STORE, LZ4, Zstandard 15/19, LZMA2 6/4 MiB and 9/8 MiB.
The value of running general-purpose codecs over already entropy-coded JPEG XL output is unmeasured; each candidate adds a full encode of up to 64 MiB per eligible object.
research_needed: Measure post-codec gain and CPU on JPEG XL outputs for a real photo corpus.

statement: Cross-file finish clears dictionaries and groups, clusters unique chunks, sorts cohorts by cohort_id, chooses Independent/Dictionary/Lookback per cohort, and sets physical order: cohort members (digest order) in cohort-ID order, then remaining chunks in digest order.
Physical chunk order is by cohort ID and digest, not by file or path, which may degrade sequential extraction locality, STREAM usability, and HTTP range coalescing.
research_needed: Measure range-request count and bytes fetched for per-file reads and sequential unpack seek/IO patterns versus file-order layout.
decision_needed: Should physical order prefer file locality for non-cohort chunks?

statement: For -v5 IDs cross-file finish drops fallbacks for reconstructive chunks, defaults other non-fast chunks to CompleteCostDidNotWin, prunes unused reconstructive plans and ReconstructionData, and toggles bit 0x4 accordingly.
Planning reports fail with Unsupported/UnknownCodec if any selected plan uses a codec other than store/v1, zstandard/v1, lz4/v1 or lzma2/v1.

V1-v3 independent selection verifies each chunk's length and SHA-256 (Corrupt ChunkDigestMismatch), stores chunks under 64 bytes, picks the smallest Zstandard candidate satisfying zstandard_wins, else STORE.
V4 independent planning verifies chunk digests and assigns each chunk the plan from select_v4_plan, counting STORE, Zstandard, LZ4, LZMA2 and transformed chunks.

V5 independent planning: per chunk, v4 selection is the baseline; non-fast profiles attempt DEFLATE recognition and compete reconstructive candidates costed with plan v2 record, ReconstructionData record and 64-byte section charge; losers record fallback reasons.
DEFLATE recognition max hash-chain length per profile: fast 512 (unused), balanced 512, dense 2048, extreme 4096.

Reconstructive candidates: balanced Zstandard 3/5; dense Zstandard 9, LZMA2 6/4 MiB, delta8->Zstandard 9; extreme Zstandard 15/19, LZMA2 9/8 MiB, delta8->Zstandard 15, byte-shuffle 2/4/8->LZMA2 9/8 MiB.
Reconstruction qualifies only if candidate + max(256, ceil(2% of baseline)) < baseline complete cost.

V4 candidates: fast STORE, LZ4, Zstd 1; balanced STORE, LZ4, Zstd 1/3/5 plus delta8 and shuffle-4 with Zstd 3; dense STORE, Zstd 5/9/15, LZMA2 4/1 MiB and 6/4 MiB plus transforms; extreme adds LZ4, Zstd 9-22, all LZMA2 pairs.

Every ordinary candidate is fully encoded for every chunk regardless of the probe (probe gates only transforms); extreme performs up to 21 full encodes per chunk (Zstd 22, LZMA2 9) plus 8 reconstructive ones, with no deterministic work budget.
evidence_in_source: code inspection; no benchmarks in repository
research_needed: Benchmark pack throughput (MiB/s) and peak memory per profile on mixed corpora up to multi-GB.
decision_needed: Is a deterministic work budget or probe-gated ordinary search required for v1 profiles?

statement: select_v4_plan: STORE is baseline; an ordinary candidate must beat STORE complete cost by the 32 B/1% margin; a transformed pipeline must beat the best ordinary cost by the same margin; strict less-than keeps earlier candidates on ties.
Dense/extreme structural candidates: delta8 and byte-shuffle 2/4/8, each with Zstandard 9 (dense) or 15 (extreme) and LZMA2 6/4 MiB; extreme adds LZMA2 9/8 MiB.

V4 complete cost charges the full canonical TransformPlan record to every chunk individually although each plan record is stored once per archive, biasing small chunks toward STORE; the effect is unmeasured.
research_needed: Compare selections and archive size using amortized plan-record cost on small-file corpora.

statement: Cohort independent baseline sums current payload bytes; for -v4/-v5 it adds each distinct plan record once per cohort (v2 length for v5) and, for v5, each referenced ReconstructionData record plus 64 bytes; v3 adds no plan cost.

Cohort baselines charge plan records that are also shared with chunks outside the cohort (overstating independent cost), while v3 baselines omit plan cost but dictionary candidates include theirs; resulting bias in dictionary/lookback selection is unmeasured.
research_needed: Recompute exact archive-size deltas for accepted and rejected cohort strategies on similarity-rich corpora.

statement: Dictionary candidate cost = all cohort payloads with the dictionary + Dictionary record + 64-byte section + plan record; it must be more than 128 bytes cheaper than independent and cheaper than any earlier candidate.

Lookback candidate per (lookback, level): each member is Zstandard prefix-coded against its preceding cohort members in digest order; cost = payloads + plan record + group record + 64; dictionary is evaluated first so ties favour independent then dictionary.

Dictionary training uses the first maximum_training_samples cohort chunks in digest order, each truncated to maximum_sample_bytes; failure yields no candidate; construction string embeds zstd-1.5.7 trainer, planner ID and caps.

Lookback prefix = concatenated plaintext of up to `lookback` preceding cohort members truncated to the final 1 MiB; declared max_preceding_bytes = maximum untruncated logical length sum of those immediate predecessors.

Every cohort member, including predecessors, is prefix-coded and random access decodes prerequisites recursively, so reading the last member transitively decodes the whole preceding cohort (up to 128 chunks), not max_lookback chunks; declared access costs understate this.
refines_or_supersedes: contradicts docs/cross-file-compression-v1.md L67-79 (access bounded by max_lookback predecessors)
evidence_in_source: inference from code; tests/random_access.rs:288-365 only asserts dependency_chunk_count > 0
research_needed: Measure dependency_chunk_count and bytes decoded when randomly reading the last member of 64- and 128-chunk cohorts.
decision_needed: Redefine declared access cost as the transitive closure, or restrict prefix chains (e.g., periodic independent members)?

statement: Cohort strategies use an absolute strict 128-byte gain rule with no relative term, regardless of cohort size.
Inserting a different Dictionary or TransformPlan under an existing ID aborts planning (Corrupt DictionaryDigestMismatch or Nonconforming DuplicateSemanticDeclaration) rather than falling back.
ChunkGroup ID = SHA-256 of 'entrybound/chunk-group/v1\0' || cohort_id || level (i32 BE) || lookback (u32 BE).

Public analyze(): samples min(len, 4096) evenly spaced bytes; likely_compressible when distinct symbols <= 192, top symbol >= 12,000 ppm, or equal consecutive samples >= 20,000 ppm; integer-only; empty input is not compressible.

For chunks longer than 4096 bytes the 'adjacent repeat' metric compares consecutive samples spaced about len/4096 bytes apart, not adjacent bytes as documented; the 192/12,000/20,000 thresholds have no cited basis and may skip winning transforms.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/codec-transform-v1.md L89-93 describes adjacent equal bytes
research_needed: Measure probe false-negative rate: chunks where a structural transform would win but the probe blocked the search.

statement: Public zstandard_wins(logical_len, encoded_len): true only if encoded + 16 + max(32, ceil(1% of logical)) < logical; STORE wins ties.

independent_encoded_len uses v4 selection only for IDs ending -v4/-v5; for current -v6 archives explain computes dictionary/lookback/ordinary savings against the v1-v3 Zstandard-only baseline the v6 planner never used.
research_needed: Compare explain savings split for v6 archives with an independently recomputed v4-candidate baseline.
decision_needed: Fix baseline selection for -v6 (and enc) planner IDs before freezing explain output?

statement: Planner arithmetic overflow and size conversions fail as PolicyRefused/ResourceLimit (EB_RESOURCE_LIMIT).

Unit test: extreme selects STORE for noise, fast selects LZ4 for small repetition, dense selects a transform for little-endian counters, extreme picks Zstd/LZMA2 for text, and dense selects LZMA2 for a repeated 1.1 MB noise block (beyond the 1 MiB Zstd window).
research_needed: Replicate selection behaviour on real data classes.

statement: Unit test: a gzip level-6 stream of 20,000 synthetic text rows yields a dense reconstructive candidate that qualifies against the complete ordinary v4 cost.
research_needed: Measure on real gzip/zlib producers.

statement: Planning is strictly sequential: no parallel candidate evaluation, chunk-level concurrency, or deterministic multi-core scheme exists in planner, chunker, codec or similarity code.
evidence_in_source: code inspection (no threads, rayon or worker settings; zstd bulk compressor default single-threaded)
research_needed: Design and verify a deterministic parallel planner; measure speedup.
decision_needed: Is deterministic parallel planning required for v1?

statement: Chunking and all planners operate on a fully materialized Archive in which every file's complete plaintext is held in memory (Chunk.plaintext); there is no streaming or bounded-memory planning path.
research_needed: Measure peak RSS versus input size for pack; design bounded staging for planning.
decision_needed: Must v1 pack inputs larger than RAM?

statement: Frozen-by-ID planner reproducibility depends on byte-identical encoder outputs from pinned zstd 1.5.7 (C, via zstd-sys), lz4_flex 0.14.0, lzma-rust2 0.20.0, preflate-rs 0.7.6 and jixel 0.2.19, because selection compares measured encoded lengths; Zstd/LZ4/LZMA2 plans do not record encoder versions.
research_needed: Cross-platform (x86-64/AArch64, SIMD/BMI2 dispatch, OS) and cross-dependency-version byte-identity tests of planned archives.
decision_needed: Record encoder versions in planner IDs, or declare reproducibility only for a pinned toolchain?

statement: The codec module contains no profile or planner logic; readers dispatch only from canonical TransformPlan data recorded in the archive.
Codec identifiers zstandard/v1, lz4/v1, lzma2/v1; Zstandard window log fixed at 20 (1 MiB window) with a 4 MiB declared working set.

Declared decoder working sets (Zstd 4 MiB, LZ4 128 KiB, LZ4 window 64 KiB) are round constants without measurement, and decoders also allocate the full logical output buffer, whose inclusion in working_set semantics is undefined.
research_needed: Measure peak decoder memory per codec/level/chunk size; define what working_set_bytes covers.
decision_needed: What exactly does DecodeRequirements.working_set_bytes bound (codec state only, or output and prefix buffers too)?

statement: Parameter magics ZP01/ZD01/ZX01 (Zstd independent/dictionary/prefix), L401, LM21; plan IDs: Zstd 1000+level, prefix 10000+(level<<8)+lookback, LZ4 20001, LZMA2 30000+preset*100+log2(dict), dictionary plans 0x8000... with 63 hash bits.
Closed parameter sets: Zstandard levels {1,3,5,9,15,19,22} only (no negative/fast levels), lookbacks {1,2,4,8}, LZMA2 (preset, dictionary) pairs (4, 1 MiB), (6, 4 MiB), (9, 8 MiB).

Dictionary format 'zstd-trained/v1'; construction prefix 'zstd-1.5.7-train-buffer-v1/'; a closed allowlist of nine construction strings for balanced/dense/extreme under -v3/-v4/-v5 IDs, none naming -v6.

Readers reject any Dictionary whose construction string (embedding creation planner ID and caps) is not in the compiled allowlist, coupling decoder acceptance to creation-policy identifiers; a future planner naming itself in construction strings requires reader changes.
refines_or_supersedes: tension with CONTRIBUTING.md L67-70 (decoder must not depend on creation profile)
research_needed: Enumerate reader-side checks that depend on planner identity; test old reader with a new construction string.
decision_needed: Should Dictionary construction be informational (not validated) so readers stay planner-agnostic?

statement: Static codec registry of exactly four registrations with format_version 1: store/v1 and zstandard/v1 (no feature bit), lz4/v1 and lzma2/v1 (require FEATURE_CODEC_TRANSFORM_V1), each with validate/encode/decode function pointers; PlanMode Independent, Dictionary, Prefix.

Any codec identifier outside the registry is refused as Unsupported/UnknownCodec (EB_CODEC_UNKNOWN); there is no Brotli, bzip2, xz/LZMA1, PPMd, DEFLATE output, LZ4 frame/HC, Zstd long-distance, or pluggable codec.
research_needed: Measure density/speed gaps versus 7z (LZMA2/PPMd), xz, Brotli and zstd --long on target corpora.
decision_needed: Which additional codecs (if any) belong in the v1 frozen portfolio?

statement: STORE plan: ID 1, identifier 'bootstrap-store-v1', empty params, zero decode requirements; Zstandard plan params are 12 bytes (magic, level i32 BE, window log 20, mode byte, 1, 0) with identifier 'zstandard-v1-level-N-window-20'.
Dictionary plans carry the Dictionary digest and a hashed plan ID; prefix plans encode lookback in parameter byte 9 and require a registered lookback.

LZ4 plan: raw lz4_flex block 'lz4-block-v1-safe-default' with exact params L401 1 0 0 0, no level or acceleration option; decode fills a buffer of exactly the logical length and rejects size mismatch.

LZMA2 plan: raw single-threaded lzma-rust2 stream with preset and dictionary from the registered pairs, automatic chunk size; decode requires the entire stored payload to be consumed and the exact logical length.

LZMA2 working_set_bytes is recomputed at validation from lzma_rust2::lzma2_get_memory_usage and must equal the serialized value, so a dependency upgrade that changes that estimate would make existing archives fail as InvalidCodecParameters.
research_needed: Add frozen test vectors for declared LZMA2 requirements; diff lzma2_get_memory_usage across lzma-rust2 versions.
decision_needed: Freeze the declared LZMA2 working-set numbers in code instead of deriving them from a dependency?

statement: with_pipeline: transforms allowed only on independent plans; plan ID = 0x6000000000000000 | 61 low bits of SHA-256 over codec, params and steps; identifier 'steps -> base'; reconstructive steps add 80 MiB (DEFLATE) or 256 MiB (JPEG) working set.

validate_plans requires at least one plan; validate_plan rebuilds the canonical plan from the registry and requires exact equality of ID, identifier, parameters, dictionary and declared decode requirements.
required_features is the codec's feature bit OR the transforms' bits; without_transforms rebuilds the base plan for explain, refusing dependent Zstandard plans.

Aggregate decode requirements take the maximum window and working set over plans, OR the flags; the archive aggregate adds the sum of all Dictionary bytes plus the largest ChunkGroup max_preceding_bytes.

The archive decoder working-set aggregate (max plan + all dictionaries + max immediate lookback bytes) is not validated against actual peak memory, including transitive lookback decoding, prefix copies, and reconstruction buffers.
research_needed: Instrument decoders to measure peak memory for worst-case archives per profile and compare with declarations.

statement: Encode entry points: independent payload, already-transformed payload for whole-object regions, dictionary, prefix and reconstruction contexts; each enforces its PlanMode and refuses mismatched context.
Zstandard frames use window log 20, long-distance matching off, no checksum, content size included, no dictionary ID, bulk single-threaded compression.

Zstandard windows above 1 MiB and long-distance matching are unavailable, so repeats more than 1 MiB apart inside 2-8 MiB chunks or across chunks are exploitable only by LZMA2, dictionaries, or bounded 1 MiB prefix lookback.
evidence_in_source: planner.rs:1964-1970 test selects LZMA2 for a repeated 1.1 MB block
research_needed: Measure gains of zstd --long / larger windows on large-file and backup corpora versus decode memory.
decision_needed: Add a larger-window or LDM Zstandard plan family in a future planner?

statement: Decode path: validate plan, codec decode to intermediate length, inverse transforms in reverse order, then ReconstructedLengthMismatch or DecompressedLengthMismatch (Corrupt) if lengths differ; dependent plans require their dictionary or prefix.
STORE requires empty parameters and no dictionary but may carry structural transforms; its decode checks the exact logical length.
Dictionary and prefix Zstandard plans cannot carry structural or reconstructive transforms; transforms combine only with independent plans.
Only Zstandard has dictionary or prefix modes; store/v1, lz4/v1 and lzma2/v1 are always Independent, so cross-file strategies never compete with an LZMA2 or LZ4 dictionary/prefix variant.

Zstd independent/dictionary decode uses bulk decompression that may accept concatenated or skippable frames, and prefix decode stops after one frame without checking leftover stored bytes, although the docs claim trailing or malformed payloads are rejected.
evidence_in_source: inference from code; no test covers trailing frames
research_needed: Craft payloads with trailing skippable/data frames and extra bytes; fuzz decode_payload for all modes.
decision_needed: Must stored payloads be canonical single frames with no trailing bytes?

statement: store, LZ4, LZMA2 and independent Zstandard refuse dictionary or prefix context; prefix encoding uses Encoder::with_ref_prefix with pledged source size and the same frame flags.
A logical length not representable as usize is PolicyRefused/ResourceLimit; any decoded length mismatch is Corrupt/DecompressedLengthMismatch.

validate_dictionary: wrong codec, format or construction -> Unsupported/UnsupportedDictionaryFormat; digest mismatch -> Corrupt/DictionaryDigestMismatch. train_dictionary needs at least two samples and nonzero capacity and wraps zstd::dict::from_samples (failure PolicyRefused/CompressionFailed).
Deterministic dictionary training is assumed from the 'zstd-1.5.7-train-buffer-v1' construction label; byte-identical ZDICT output across platforms, CPU features and builds is untested.
research_needed: Cross-platform training byte-identity test on fixed sample sets.

statement: Strict parameter parsing: Zstandard params exactly 12 bytes with window log 20 and fixed flag bytes, mode chosen by magic with reserved-byte checks; LZMA2 params exactly 12 bytes, LM21, zero reserved bytes, registered pair; violations are InvalidCodecParameters.

Codec diagnostics: invalid parameters Nonconforming EB_CODEC_INVALID_PARAMETERS; compression failure PolicyRefused EB_CODEC_COMPRESSION_FAILED; decompression failure Corrupt EB_CODEC_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.

Codec unit tests: Zstd level-3 round trip; parameter tampering rejected; LZ4, LZMA2, delta8 and shuffle plans round trip; malformed LZ4/LZMA2 payloads typed; length mismatch typed; dictionary and prefix modes round trip.

Exact dependency pins: zstd =0.13.3 (zstd-sys 2.0.16+zstd.1.5.7, C code), lz4_flex =0.14.0 safe encode/decode, lzma-rust2 =0.20.0 with std/encoder/xz, preflate-rs =0.7.6, jixel =0.2.19, jxl-oxide =0.12.6, crc32fast =1.5.0, aes =0.9.3.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/codec-transform-v1.md L40-41 says lzma-rust2 enables only std and encoder (xz also enabled)

statement: Zstandard encoding and decoding rely on the C libzstd via zstd-sys while the workspace forbids unsafe Rust only in Entrybound's own crates; an independent safe-Rust reader would need a separate Zstandard decoder.
research_needed: Verify a pure-Rust Zstandard decoder (e.g., ruzstd) decodes all zstandard/v1 plan modes including ref-prefix frames.
decision_needed: Is a C dependency acceptable for the normative decoder path, and must a pure-Rust decoder be proven?

statement: Transform identifiers delta8/v1 and byte-shuffle/v1; ReversibilityClass Structural or Reconstructive; ReconstructionBacking SideData or SelfContained.

Closed transform registry: delta8/v1 and byte-shuffle/v1 (Structural, bit 0x2), deflate-reconstruct/v1 (Reconstructive, SideData, bit 0x4), jpeg-jxl-reconstruct/v1 (Reconstructive, SelfContained, bit 0x8).

Unregistered transforms fail as Unsupported/UnknownTransform (EB_TRANSFORM_UNKNOWN); there are no BCJ/executable filters, multi-byte or distance deltas, floating-point or record-aware transforms, or embedded DEFLATE (PNG/ZIP/PDF) reconstruction.
research_needed: Measure potential gains of BCJ, delta-N and format-aware transforms on executables, tables, and document corpora.
decision_needed: Which additional transforms justify registry growth for v1?

statement: Pipeline rules: structural steps never reference ReconstructionData; at most one reconstructive step, which must be first and match its backing (SideData needs a reference, SelfContained forbids one); no transform identifier may repeat.
Pipelines cannot nest reconstruction (for example DEFLATE inside ZIP inside JPEG) or repeat a transform family (such as two deltas or shuffles of different widths).

Forward pipeline: structural steps must preserve length (Corrupt TransformedLengthMismatch); SideData steps re-run verified DEFLATE forward against recorded data; SelfContained steps re-run verified JPEG forward, with ineligibility reported as Nonconforming TransformFailed.
A pipeline containing a ReconstructionData reference cannot be encoded or decoded without the recorded ReconstructionData map (Nonconforming UnknownReconstructionData).

Inverse pipeline applies steps in reverse order (preflate recreation or JPEG XL reconstruction for reconstructive steps); the codec's intermediate length comes from the first step's ReconstructionData.
delta8/v1 has empty parameters and emits byte minus previous (mod 256) from a zero seed; byte-shuffle/v1 width is exactly 2, 4 or 8, emits lanes of complete records and copies the tail unchanged.
Transform diagnostics: InvalidTransformParameters (Nonconforming, EB_TRANSFORM_INVALID_PARAMETERS) and TransformedLengthMismatch (Corrupt, EB_TRANSFORM_LENGTH_MISMATCH).

deflate-reconstruct/v1 constants: format 'preflate-rs-0.7.6/deflate-reconstruct-v1'; max input 16 MiB; max side data 16 MiB; max intermediate 64 MiB; declared working set 80 MiB; expansion ratio 64; side-data magic ERD1 with 24-byte header.
The 80 MiB reconstruction working set, 64 MiB intermediate cap and 64x expansion bound are not measured against preflate-rs peak memory or real stream expansion.
research_needed: Measure preflate-rs peak memory and expansion on real zlib/gzip corpora at each max-chain setting.

statement: Reconstruction parameters are 'DR01' plus max chain length (u32 BE); only 512, 2048 or 4096 are valid (InvalidTransformParameters otherwise).

try_forward: empty or >16 MiB input is ineligible; recognize wrapper; preflate with verify_compression and 64 MiB plaintext limit; require complete raw consumption, expansion bound, wrapper checksum and side data <=16 MiB; ineligible returns None, not an error.
Reconstruction requires both SHA-256 equality and byte-for-byte equality between original and recreated bytes; the check cannot be disabled.

verified_forward (writer path) re-runs recognition and requires identical ReconstructionData (Corrupt ReconstructionDataDigestMismatch) and exact recreation (Corrupt ReconstructedDigestMismatch), so unverified caller data cannot be committed.

inverse checks format, bounds, digest and side-data shape, requires the declared intermediate length, recreates via preflate, caps output at 16 MiB and re-checks wrapper checksums; unknown format is Unsupported UnsupportedReconstructionFormat.

Decoding requires preflate-rs 0.7.6 correction-stream semantics identified only by a format string; no independent specification of the correction format exists, so long-term and independent-reader decodability depends on that crate.
research_needed: Assess preflate-rs correction-format stability across versions; attempt decoding with a second implementation.
decision_needed: Vendor and specify the correction format, or accept dependency-defined decoding for reconstructive archives?

statement: Recognition: gzip by 1F8B magic with bounded header (FEXTRA, FNAME, FCOMMENT, FHCRC; reserved flags zero); zlib by CM=8, CINFO<=7 and FCHECK with FDICT ineligible; any other chunk is attempted as raw DEFLATE.
No scanning for embedded DEFLATE (PNG, ZIP, PDF, OOXML), no multi-member gzip, no preset-dictionary zlib, and no streams crossing chunk boundaries; such inputs fall back to ordinary encoding.
research_needed: Quantify DEFLATE-embedded bytes (PNG/ZIP/OOXML/PDF) in target corpora and achievable gains.
decision_needed: Should embedded-DEFLATE reconstruction be in scope for v1?

statement: DEFLATE reconstruction runs per CDC Chunk, so compressed files larger than one chunk (balanced cuts from 128 KiB, forced at 2 MiB) are split and never recognized; tests build single whole-file chunks or small files.
evidence_in_source: inference from code; test fixtures bypass CDC
research_needed: Pack real .gz/.tgz/.zlib corpora through pack_directory and measure fraction of DEFLATE bytes reconstructed.
decision_needed: Add whole-object DEFLATE regions (like v6 JPEG) before freezing v1?

statement: Raw-DEFLATE parsing is attempted with preflate on every non-fast chunk that is not gzip or zlib, with unmeasured CPU cost on incompressible or non-DEFLATE data.
research_needed: Benchmark per-chunk recognition time on random, text and media chunks.

statement: Wrapper checksums validated (Adler-32 for zlib; CRC-32 and ISIZE for gzip); side data encodes wrapper kind, prefix, corrections and suffix with exact lengths, and decoding enforces canonical wrapper shapes.

Eligibility and correctness evidence covers only flate2-generated raw/zlib/gzip streams at levels 4 and 6 over one synthetic text; real producers (zlib levels 1-9, libdeflate, 7-Zip, zopfli, pigz) and correction overhead are unmeasured.
research_needed: Corpus study across DEFLATE producers measuring recognition rate, correction size and net savings.

statement: jpeg-jxl-reconstruct/v1 constants: canonical parameters pin jixel 0.2.19, jxl-oxide 0.12.6 and threads=1; limits JPEG 64 MiB, JXL 64 MiB, 100,000,000 pixels, 256 MiB working set, 4096 region chunks, expansion 64; REGION_MEMBER_PLAN_REF = 0.
REGION_MEMBER_PLAN_REF (0) has the same value as the planner's UNPLANNED_PLAN_ID (0), so plan_ref 0 means either unplanned or region-owned and must be disambiguated by region membership.
research_needed: Conformance tests: non-region chunk with plan_ref 0 in INDEXED and STREAM layouts must be rejected.
decision_needed: Use a distinct sentinel for region membership before format freeze?

statement: verified_forward: size cap, marker scan, SOF0 required, pixel bound, jixel lossless transcode with one thread and reconstruction data inside catch_unwind, JXL size cap, jxl-oxide inverse, then SHA-256 and byte equality.
Only baseline SOF0 JPEGs are attempted; extended sequential (SOF1), progressive (SOF2), lossless, hierarchical and arithmetic-coded JPEGs are reported Unsupported and fall back.
research_needed: Measure prevalence of non-SOF0 JPEGs in camera, web and archive corpora.
decision_needed: Is progressive JPEG support required for v1 claims?

statement: A valid progressive JPEG from jpeg-encoder exposes an internal failure in the pinned jixel/jxl-oxide forward stack, which is why v1 rejects progressive SOF markers before calling the dependency.
research_needed: Minimize and report the upstream failure; retest newer versions.

statement: Recognition requires the object to start with FFD8 and end exactly with FFD9, so JPEGs with trailing data after EOI (appended metadata, MPF, motion-photo video, padding) are NotRecognized.
research_needed: Measure share of real-world JPEGs with post-EOI data.
decision_needed: Support trailing-data JPEGs via prefix/suffix side data?

statement: Bounded marker parser skips fill bytes and standalone markers, stops at SOS or EOI, reads dimensions from the first SOF segment, and rejects invalid lengths; it does not scan nested JPEG streams.

Dependency panics are unwind-confined, but aborts, OOM, stack overflow and unbounded CPU time are not contained; the jixel encoder has no allocation tracker, so large-pixel inputs may exhaust memory during packing.
research_needed: Fuzz jixel and jxl-oxide paths; measure encoder peak memory versus megapixels; test panic=abort builds.
decision_needed: Is in-process execution of JPEG XL transcoding acceptable, or is isolation or a lower pixel cap required?

statement: Reconstruction (read path) caps JXL size, uses a jxl-oxide AllocTracker of 256 MiB, bounds pixels, requires JPEG reconstruction status Available, and writes through a 64 MiB bounded writer; failures are Corrupt MalformedReconstructionPayload or ResourceLimit.
The largest JPEG reconstructable within the 256 MiB allocation tracker is unknown, so the 100 MP pixel cap may be unreachable and large photos may fail verification; limits lack measurement.
research_needed: Measure jxl-oxide reconstruction memory versus image dimensions and chroma subsampling.

statement: Decoding v6 regions depends on jxl-oxide JPEG bitstream reconstruction with version-pinned canonical parameters; whether other JPEG XL decoders (e.g., libjxl) recreate identical JPEG bytes is unverified.
research_needed: Cross-decoder test: reconstruct stored representations with libjxl djxl and compare bytes.
decision_needed: Is dependency-version-pinned JPEG reconstruction acceptable for long-term archives?

statement: Region identity = SHA-256 over 'entrybound/reconstruction-region/jpeg-jxl/v1\0', content object, chunk range, plan, byte counts, access cost fields and the representation digest.

JPEG evidence uses only synthetic images (image and jpeg-encoder crates, up to 1024x1024); metadata-marker tests accept either exact success or fallback, so real eligibility rate and savings are unmeasured.
research_needed: Corpus study of camera/web JPEGs: eligibility, verification failures, net savings, time and memory.

statement: The default balanced-v6 profile only considers single-chunk JPEG objects; with BALANCED_V2 cutting from 128 KiB and forced at 2 MiB, most multi-megabyte photos are excluded, so the default rarely gains from JPEG reconstruction.
research_needed: Measure fraction of JPEG bytes eligible under balanced on photo corpora.
decision_needed: Accept independent-chunk access over JPEG savings for the default profile?

statement: Whole-object JPEG regions declare worst reconstructed bytes equal to the region's logical bytes: reading any member chunk reconstructs the entire JPEG.
Similarity is only a bounded creation-time planning hint; SHA-256 remains the sole authority for exact chunk equality and no fingerprint enters identity or decoding.
bottom-k-shingle-v1: 32-byte shingles at 16-byte stride, at most 4096 scanned shingles per chunk, FNV-1a-64 with offset cbf29ce484222325 and prime 00000100000001b3.

Frozen similarity policies: fast disabled; balanced k8, threshold 500, cohorts 8-32, 64 candidates, 8 KiB dictionary, 16x16 KiB samples; dense k16, 375, 4-64, 128, 16 KiB, 32x32 KiB; extreme k32, 250, 3-128, 256, 32 KiB, 64x64 KiB.
Sketch sizes, thresholds, cohort bounds, candidate caps, dictionary sizes and sample caps are frozen without cited measurement.
research_needed: Parameter sweep measuring cohort quality, dictionary/lookback savings and planning time on similarity-rich corpora (source trees, logs, JSON, VM images).

statement: cluster(): greedy pass over digest-ordered unique chunks; candidate cohorts found via sketch-value buckets up to the cap; full cohorts skipped; join the cohort whose leader shares the most sketch values (ties: lowest cohort_id) if shared*1000 >= min(sketch sizes)*threshold; otherwise start a new cohort; drop cohorts below minimum.

Resemblance is estimated by intersecting two independent bottom-k sketches against the cohort leader only, divided by the smaller sketch size, which is not a standard unbiased Jaccard estimator; greedy digest-order assignment is order-dependent.
research_needed: Compare cohort recall/precision and resulting savings against exact resemblance, MinHash-LSH, SimHash or file-type grouping baselines.

statement: For chunks over about 65 KiB shingles are sampled at fixed stride multiples from the chunk start, so shifted but similar content may yield disjoint sketches; recall on 256 KiB-8 MiB chunks is unmeasured.
research_needed: Measure sketch overlap for large chunks with small insertions or offsets.

statement: Cohort ID = SHA-256 of 'entrybound/similarity-cohort/v1\0' || policy_id length (u64 BE) || policy_id || leader chunk digest.
Unit tests: ten 64 KiB chunks with localized single-byte edits form one deterministic balanced cohort; unrelated noise forms none; structured text clusters from content, not names.
Similarity, dictionaries and deduplication are scoped to a single archive's chunk map; there are no cross-archive dictionaries, reference archives or cross-archive dedup.
decision_needed: Is cross-archive dedup or dictionary reuse in scope after v1?

statement: Encrypted packing runs the same v6 planner over plaintext: per-chunk compression, trained shared dictionaries, bounded lookback and similarity cohorts mixing files; resulting ciphertext sizes may leak cross-file content relationships (compression side channel).
evidence_in_source: code inspection; no mitigation in planner
research_needed: Security analysis of size leakage with padding schedules; experiments with attacker-chosen files co-packed with secrets.
decision_needed: Should encrypted mode disable cross-file dictionaries/lookback or require padding to bound leakage?

statement: Chunking is creation-time only; decoders never invoke the chunker and consume recorded ordered Chunk references.
CDC cost constants: CHUNK_FRAME_OVERHEAD_BYTES 64, INDEX_ENTRY_OVERHEAD_BYTES 100, CHUNK_REFERENCE_OVERHEAD_BYTES 40.

The 64-byte frame charge matches only version-1 chunk frames; all v3+ archives use 96-byte extended frames and v5/v6 add per-chunk and per-object audit records, so CDC selection underestimates per-chunk overhead; the 100-byte Index figure is unverified.
research_needed: Measure actual per-unique-chunk and per-reference bytes in v6 INDEXED and STREAM archives and whether corrected costs change selection.
decision_needed: Introduce a new chunk-selection version with corrected overhead constants?

statement: Gear table: 256 u64 values table[i] = splitmix64(0x6a09e667f3bcc909 + i); PHTE constants: modulus 2^127-1 and a 64-byte rolling window.
EncryptedBoundaryKey is creation-time only and never serialized: SecretGearTable (256 keyed u64) or PhteAes128 (field polynomial plus AES-128 key).

Public ChunkingParameters (chunker_id, minimum, target, maximum), ChunkRange (start, end) and ChunkingEvaluation (parameters, estimated cost, unique chunk count, manifest references, unique plaintext bytes).

Four frozen gear-norm-v1 policies (min/target/max): FAST_V2 512 KiB/2 MiB/8 MiB, BALANCED_V2 128 KiB/512 KiB/2 MiB, DENSE_V2 64 KiB/256 KiB/1 MiB, EXTREME_V2 32 KiB/128 KiB/512 KiB, with chunker_id 'gear-norm-v1/min-N/target-N/max-N'.
Chunk size policies (targets 128 KiB to 2 MiB) are chosen without cited measurements of dedup ratio, compression ratio, metadata overhead, or random-access granularity.
research_needed: Sweep chunk sizes on versioned backup, source-tree and VM-image corpora versus FastCDC/restic/borg defaults.

statement: gear-norm-v1: hash resets at each chunk start, hash = (hash << 1) + table[byte]; no cut before minimum; before target cut when low (b+1) bits are zero, from target when low (b-1) bits are zero; forced cut at maximum; trailing chunk may be short; empty input has no chunks.

Boundaries test the low-order bits of a Gear hash, where bit k depends only on the last k+1 bytes, so the effective window is about 20 bytes for a 512 KiB target (no FastCDC-style spread mask); short-period content may never cut; real-data resynchronization is unmeasured.
evidence_in_source: synthetic insertion test on noise only (tests/cdc_dedup.rs:32-52)
research_needed: Compare boundary distribution and dedup resync with FastCDC 2020 masks on low-entropy and periodic corpora.
decision_needed: Accept low-bit masks for frozen gear-norm-v1 or introduce a successor chunker?

statement: Encrypted CDC: SecretGearTable reuses gear-norm with a keyed table; PHTE computes a 64-byte rolling polynomial hash over GF(2^127-1), encrypts the state with AES-128 per byte past the minimum, and applies the same masks; its rolling state is not reset at boundaries.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/chunking-v1.md L103-106 (still states keyed/encrypted boundaries unsupported)

statement: No security analysis in code supports the keyed boundary constructions: chunk lengths visible via ciphertext sizes may leak plaintext structure, and a secret Gear table with low-bit masks may be recoverable from chosen-plaintext boundaries.
research_needed: Formal/security analysis and attack experiments on keyed Gear and PHTE boundary leakage; external review.
decision_needed: Which boundary mode is the v1 default for encrypted archives, and is keyed Gear acceptable at all?

statement: A PHTE polynomial that is not a canonical field element (>= 2^127-1) is refused as PolicyRefused/ResourceLimit.
PHTE performs bit-serial u128 field multiplications (up to 127 iterations each) and one AES block per byte, likely far slower than Gear; encrypted packing throughput is unmeasured.
research_needed: Benchmark MiB/s of gear-norm, secret-table and PHTE chunking across CPUs.

statement: select_parameters(_encrypted) fully chunks and SHA-256-hashes all contents for each candidate and keeps the lowest estimated cost (earlier wins ties); an empty candidate list is a ResourceLimit refusal.
evaluate: identical whole contents (by SHA-256) are counted once; estimated cost = unique plaintext bytes + 164 bytes per unique chunk + 40 bytes per manifest chunk reference.

CDC selection uses uncompressed unique bytes as its proxy, ignoring codec, dictionary, lookback and reconstruction effects of chunk size; whether it selects the policy with smallest final archive is unmeasured.
research_needed: For each corpus, pack with every chunking candidate end-to-end and compare against the proxy's choice.

statement: CDC parameters must satisfy 0 < minimum <= target <= maximum with target a power of two >= 2 (Nonconforming ResourceLimit); ranges must be contiguous, non-empty, <= maximum, only the last below minimum, and cover all input (Nonconforming SectionStructure).
Integration test: after a 4 KiB insertion into 12 MiB of noise, BALANCED_V2 CDC recovers at least three downstream chunks and more than fixed 512 KiB blocks.
research_needed: Repeat on real edited-file corpora.

statement: Integration tests: chunking changes PCR but not ContentObject digest, LAI or AUX; archive-wide exact dedup is deterministic and corruption of a shared STORE chunk is localized by digest; denser chunking wins only when dedup beats overhead; historical fixed-1mib/v1 archives still open.

replan_archive records chunker_id 'entrybound/gear-cdc-v1/min-.../target-.../max-...' while pack records 'gear-norm-v1/min-...' for the same algorithm; since PCR binds chunker_id, replanning identical content yields a different PCR and a non-frozen identifier.
refines_or_supersedes: contradicts docs/chunking-v1.md L45-49 and chunker.rs:78-108 chunker_id strings
evidence_in_source: code inspection; no test asserts replan chunker_id
research_needed: Test PCR and chunker_id equality between pack_directory and replan_archive for identical input.
decision_needed: Correct replan to record gear-norm-v1 IDs before freezing identity semantics?

statement: The chunker API accepts only complete in-memory byte slices; there is no incremental or streaming CDC interface, and selection re-reads all contents once per candidate.

Integration tests: balanced packs mix STORE and Zstandard per chunk with exact round trip and planner balanced-v6; repeated packs are byte-identical for all four profiles on the same machine and record a candidate chunker_id.
research_needed: Cross-machine determinism runs.

statement: Integration tests: dense v4 transform pipeline round-trips through INDEXED and STREAM with equal LAI/AUX/PCR; missing feature bit and unknown transform are refused; profiles leave LAI/AUX unchanged; balanced declares 1 MiB window and 4 MiB working set, refused before decompression under smaller policy.

Integration test: corrupted compressed payload, wrong logical length, unknown codec and altered codec parameters yield DecompressionFailed, DecompressedLengthMismatch, UnknownCodec and InvalidCodecParameters.

Integration test: 24 similar 64 KiB files under balanced yield one shared dictionary <= 8 KiB backing >= 8 chunks, no lookback, deterministic bytes, savings attribution that sums, and typed UnknownDictionary/UnsupportedDictionaryFormat refusals.

Integration test: dense/extreme select lookback <= 4/<= 8 on similar files while LAI, AUX and PCR match balanced; working set exceeds 4 MiB and is enforced; tampered group refs, access costs and ordering are refused.
Integration test: tiny similar files stay independent with an explained reason; historical v3 and v2 planners still produce verifiable archives with only the expected feature bits.

Integration tests: v5 dense reconstruction of a gzip fixture round-trips with identical LAI/AUX/PCR to v4, survives STREAM layout, fails typed when data is missing, corrupt or undeclared, and records UnrecognizedOrVerificationFailed fallbacks visible in explain.
evidence_in_source: integration tests with single whole-file chunk fixtures

statement: Integration tests: dense v6 selects one multi-chunk JPEG region with deterministic bytes and unchanged LAI/AUX/PCR, enforces region validation codes, survives STREAM, requires >128 MiB working set, balanced falls back for small JPEG, and shared chunks make regions ineligible.

Random-access tests read dictionary-backed and lookback-grouped entries and a DEFLATE-reconstructed entry with verification; the lookback test asserts only that dependency_chunk_count is positive, not that it is bounded by max_lookback.
research_needed: Add assertions bounding dependency counts and bytes against declared access costs.

statement: STREAM layout tests show shared dictionaries and bounded lookback groups survive the sequential layout.

The workspace has only the entrybound and entrybound-cli crates: no fuzz targets for codec, transform, preflate or JPEG XL decode paths and no benchmark harness for planner, chunker or codec throughput.
evidence_in_source: workspace manifest; no fuzz or bench directories
research_needed: Add cargo-fuzz targets for decode_payload modes, ReconstructionData, JXL reconstruction; add deterministic benchmark suite.
decision_needed: Is fuzzing of all attacker-facing decoders a v1 release gate?

statement: Bootstrap CLI decode policy allows an 8 MiB window (exactly the LZMA2 preset-9 dictionary) and a 384 MiB working set (to admit the 256 MiB JPEG XL reconstruction set); the resource policy is described as deliberately generous and experimental.
research_needed: Validate defaults against measured worst-case decoder memory per profile.
decision_needed: What default decode policy should v1 readers ship?

statement: Encrypted boundary keys derive from the key hierarchy: a secret Gear table from HMAC outputs (chunker prefix 'gear-norm-secret-table-v1') or a PHTE polynomial by rejection sampling plus AES key (prefix 'phte-aes128-norm-v1'); CDC min/target/max come from the same profile candidates.
